routines.name: LIMIT: exponent range
routines.desc: Twenty multiplications by 16 million reach 1.1e72 - close to the machine's ceiling of about 7.2e75. Beyond it the exponent overflows and the program is interrupted.

routines.name: LIMIT: 4.3e9 + 1
routines.desc: Adding one to a large number and subtracting it again returns ZERO. Past about 16 million, the gap between representable numbers exceeds 1, so the addition simply vanishes - 24 bits of fraction is the whole budget.

routines.name: LIMIT: 0.1 x 10
routines.desc: The machine stores fractions in hexadecimal, and 0.1 is not exactly representable - so ten additions land at 0.9999996, not 1. Every Shuttle computation carried this kind of drift; the software was written to expect it.
